claims.text: As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal strain of approximately 13.5%.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 contains a continuous ordered phase.
The continuous ordered phase causes brittleness under tensile loading in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Annealing HfZrTiTa0.53 near 600 °C for 20–120 hours will partially disorder and decompose its continuous ordered phase.
The anneal will produce a continuous disordered BCC matrix containing discrete nanoscale ordered precipitates in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The annealed microstructure may contain oxygen-induced ordered complexes.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix will increase dislocation mobility.
The continuous disordered BCC matrix will delay deformation localization.
Discrete ordered precipitates will sustain load transfer and help preserve high strength.
The discrete precipitates will permit rapid impact-triggered energy release.
The annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the baseline alloy.
Uniform tensile elongation will increase from approximately 13.5% to more than 20%.
The annealed alloy will retain a yield strength near 786 MPa.
The annealed alloy will retain impact-triggered energy-release behavior comparable to the baseline.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration may cause grain growth or precipitate coarsening.
Anneal-induced grain growth or precipitate coarsening may degrade strength.
The predicted ductility effect is applicable at room temperature under quasi-static tension at approximately 1×10^-3 s^-1.
Conducting the anneal under an inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% terminal strain is described ambiguously as tensile or compressive and is then treated as the baseline uniform tensile elongation. Terminal compressive strain and uniform tensile elongation are not interchangeable quantities.

The prediction permits yield strength to remain merely 'near' 786 MPa, whereas the falsification rule treats any degradation relative to baseline as falsifying, imposing a stricter criterion than the stated prediction.
